subject: Pinecrest — pricing alignment & migration considerations
messages:
From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Linden <sarah@pinecrest.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Pinecrest — pricing alignment & migration considerations

Hi Sarah,

Thanks again for taking the demo yesterday — really appreciated the time. From our side, a couple of items popped up that your team said would be critical to decide whether a move makes sense: clear price parity or credits to offset migration, an onboarding SLA for latency-sensitive endpoints, and packaging that supports your burst-y usage patterns.

Could you share the current contract economics (list pricing + any committed monthly spend) and any timing constraints for a decision? If you prefer, we can propose two concrete options: (A) match the core per-token economics you have today and offer a 12-week onboarding credit, or (B) a blended discount plus dedicated ramp credits tied to usage.

Either way, I want to make sure we map to Pinecrest's procurement requirements so any counteroffer is actionable. Happy to set a short call with Ben and our solutions lead next week.

Best,
Ava Chen
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ava.chen@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0182
Redwood Inference
From: Sarah Linden <sarah@pinecrest.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Pinecrest Procurement <procurement@pinecrest.com>
Date: 2027-04-19T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pinecrest — pricing alignment & migration considerations

Ava,

Appreciate the follow-up. We are evaluating Redwood alongside EdgeCloud. High level: they currently have a slightly lower per-token list price for our high-volume endpoints but Redwood's performance looked promising for our low-latency use cases. Procurement asked that any competitive conversation include: a) explicit price match (per-token + embeddings), b) migration/onboarding credits, c) representative T&Cs for data residency and SLAs.

I've attached our RFP answers and current contract summary to give you context (see Pinecrest_RFP_Answers_v1.pdf). We would ideally have a commercial term sheet by EOD Friday 4/23 to brief leadership on Monday.

Can Ben provide a term-sheet that shows the tradeoffs between a straight match vs. a credits-based onramp? Also copying procurement to flag timing.

Thanks,
Sarah Linden
Head of Platform Partnerships
Pinecrest Technologies

Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-19T15:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pinecrest — pricing alignment & migration considerations

Sarah, Ava — thanks for the context. I've pulled together an initial price-match term sheet (attached) with two parallel options:

- Option 1 — Straight match: match EdgeCloud's published per-token price for the first 12 months, standard hosted SLA, no onboarding credit.
- Option 2 — Mixed: 15% off list for first year + $60k onboarding credit over first 90 days (applied as post-bill credits) + dedicated onboarding support (1 solutions engineer, 4 weeks).

Notes and assumptions: we assume Pinecrest will move at least 70% of the endpoints listed in the RFP within the first 3 months to qualify for the onboarding credit. We also need to confirm usual termination and data export clauses; finance will want to cap the total one-time credits to avoid open-ended exposure.

I've attached price-match-term-sheet.xlsx with line-item math. If procurement prefers a straight match we can push on margin via a volume-based true-up (Q3 usage-based rebate) instead of upfront credits.

Ava, can we schedule a 30-minute alignment with procurement on Thursday 4/22?

Ben Carter
Director, Sales — Strategic Accounts
ben.carter@redwood.ai | +1 (650) 555-0234

Folks — quick technical/packaging notes to feed into the commercial: 

• Packaging: recommend a two-line product bundle for Pinecrest — (1) latency-critical hosted inference at a reserved-QPS tier, (2) burst-friendly on-demand tier. Pricing should reflect reserved baseline with discounted overage buckets.

• Migration credits: prefer credits tied to verified endpoint cutover (we can instrument a migration report to confirm traffic shift). This avoids customers taking credits without moving traffic.

• Data residency & SLAs: we can commit to regionally pinned inference endpoints + audit logs; we will need a short annex for the SLA window they care about.

On the timeline, a Thursday alignment works; I suggest we bring a short onboarding playbook and a sample migration acceptance checklist.

Stephanie Nguyen
Solutions Lead, Customer Success
stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai

Sarah, procurement team — thanks for the patience while we finalized approvals. Attached is our formal offer. Highlights: 

• Commercial: 20% off list for the first 12 months for the reserved baseline (applies to both generation and embeddings), plus a $60,000 onboarding credit applied over the first 90 days.
• Eligibility: credit applies when at least 65% of RFP-listed endpoints are live on Redwood and region-pinning is configured per the acceptance checklist.
• SLA & T&Cs: we will include a short SLA appendix covering 99.5% availability for reserved endpoints and audit log access for compliance.

Next steps: if the term sheet looks good, procurement can sign the attached DocuSign and we will stand up a kickoff: solutions engineer + implementation plan + migration acceptance checklist. We can also include a Q3 usage true-up rebate if Pinecrest prefers long-term volume anchors instead of the upfront credit.

I've attached pinecrest-offer-20270423.pdf (redlined copy for DocuSign). Please confirm if procurement wants the pricing numbers broken by endpoint group and I'll send the line-item export from the deal.

Regards,
Priyom Das
